transcript:
Meeting Header: 2028-12-05 10:00 PT / 13:00 ET - Duration: 48m
Attendees: Sara Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Rosa Alvarez (Redwood SE), Jenna Morales (BlueMarble Head of Data), Tom Rivera (BlueMarble Platform), Priya Singh (BlueMarble CTO), Ethan Cole (BlueMarble ML)

Summary: Quick integration discovery focused on SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex workflows, gateway/proxy patterns, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Customer evaluating hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) for latency-sensitive search and e-commerce completion features.

Topics: 1) SDK support + LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors 2) Gateway/proxy and on-prem proxying options 3) Rate limits / quotas / per-route throttling 4) Observability / traces / token-level cost 5) Security: VPC, KMS, SOC2, audit logs 6) Next steps / PoC plan

Transcript: 
00:00 Sara: ok everyone good, we're gonna kick off - thanks for making time. I'm sara patel from Redwood, and with me is liam and rosa, our SEs. who should we start with on the blue marble side for intros?
00:08 Jenna: hey, this is jenna, head of data. priya is our cto and tom runs platform. ethan is the ml engineer working on the prompt infra. quick call, we want to validate integration effort and security fit before a pilot.
00:18 Sara: perfect, high level - are you leaning hosted, dedicated or private at this stage?
00:22 Priya: leaning dedicated or private. we need predictable latency for search autocomplete and cart suggestions, can't have a noisy neighbor issue during peak sales. also, data residency for eu customers.
00:33 Liam: makes sense - dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput; private (vpc/on-prem) is for strict compliance. hosted still viable if you can tolerate multi-tenant and we handle routing and fallbacks.
00:42 Tom: two practical things for us - 1) how do we integrate with existing codebase (we use node + python microservices), 2) what does routing through our gateway look like? we operate an edge gateway/proxy today.
00:55 Rosa: we have official SDKs for python and node, and our HTTP REST endpoints are straightforward. for node there's a lightweight streaming client, and we provide sample wrappers for langchain, llamaindex, and other orchestration libs.
01:08 Ethan: quick question on langchain - do you have maintained connectors or do we adapt examples?
01:12 Liam: we maintain official LangChain agents/examples and a LlamaIndex connector. they're in github, examples for retriever-augmented generation (RAG), chains, and prompt templates. some customers customize; we show a minimal adapter you can drop into your chain.
01:26 Jenna: any existing customers using LlamaIndex at scale?
01:29 Liam: yes a few - we did a POC with a retail customer using llamaindex for semantic search. caveat: name transcription sometimes appears in our docs as LlamaIdx or L-index in quick notes, but the repo is LlamaIndex.
01:41 Priya: for our infra, we use an internal API gateway. we prefer not to disclose keys to outside services - can we route via an internal proxy so requests appear to originate from our VPC?
01:50 Rosa: yes - two patterns: 1) customers proxy requests through their gateway to hosted Redwood API (we accept inbound from your IP ranges), 2) for Private deployments we install the runtime inside your VPC/on-prem so no external egress for inference. both support KMS and audit logging.
02:06 Tom: if we proxy, does Redwood do any IP-level allowlist or mTLS?
02:10 Liam: we support IP allowlisting and mutual TLS for dedicated/private. for hosted we also have per-api-key restrictions and org-level policies.
02:18 Ethan: about rate limits - how flexible are quotas? we have bursty traffic and need burst capacity without sudden 429s during flash sales.
02:25 Liam: quotas are per-account and per-route. for Dedicated you get configurable autoscaling and burst policies. Hosted has rate limits and quota tiers; we can configure burst windows and graceful backpressure - also automatic fallback to smaller model variants if you opt in.
02:39 Priya: graceful degradation is important. If the primary model is full we'd rather fall back to a cheaper variant with slightly higher latency than errors. is that the default?
02:46 Rosa: fallback is policy-driven; we can automatically route to pinned compatible variants, or queue requests. for critical paths we recommend Dedicated with reserved throughput + fallback policies.
02:56 Jenna: what about observability - we need traces and token-level cost per request for our billing team. do you expose hooks?
03:03 Liam: yes - Redwood Console gives per-route and per-model dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, and tracing hooks. we also surface x-trace-id and allow you to pass a client request id to correlate with your logs. webhooks for inference events and an ingest for OpenTelemetry traces are supported.
03:19 Tom: can we push spans to our jaeger/otel collector or do you integrate?
03:23 Liam: we support OpenTelemetry exporters - if you're on Dedicated or Private you can stream traces to your collector. For Hosted you can export logs and traces via webhooks or a secure log export; dedicated has direct streaming options.
03:36 Priya: curious about per-token pricing visibility - our finance team needs line-item costs per request, ideally broken out by prompt vs completion tokens.
03:43 Sara: console shows that breakdown, plus you can export daily CSVs with per-request token counts and costs. we also provide a rate-limited usage API if you want automated billing reconciliation.
03:53 Jenna: integration complexity - how much effort to replace calls in our code? we currently call openai style endpoints; would swapping to Redwood be small?
04:01 Rosa: typically small - SDKs mirror common OpenAI patterns (request body fields similar), plus we have middleware snippets for express/fastify and python flask/fastapi. for streaming responses we supply event-stream compatible clients.
04:14 Ethan: one more: LangChain retriever pipelines - do you host vector DBs or recommend connectors?
04:19 Liam: we integrate with common vector DBs (Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate, FAISS via on-prem connectors). for Hosted we sometimes offer managed vector options, but most customers host their own and we provide connectors and examples for lazy indexing with LlamaIndex.
04:32 Priya: we have strict audit needs - SOC2 and ISO are required, plus we need KMS integration for keys and a full request audit log. do you provide that?
04:40 Sara: yes - Redwood has SOC2 Type II, ISO attestation. For Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM, detailed audit logs (request/response meta), and exportable compliance artifacts. we'll attach our security pack in follow-up.
04:53 Tom: does the audit log contain full request/response or masked content? legal wants minimal PII retention.
04:58 Rosa: logs are configurable - you can mask or redact portions, we can disable response body retention, and we support configurable retention windows. Private gives you full control.
05:08 Jenna: good. on quotas again, if we do dedicated what level of SLAs are we looking at?
05:13 Liam: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets per contract, and reserved capacity guarantees. We'll size GPUs based on your QPS and token lengths; Rosa can send a sizing example.
05:22 Sara: for a PoC, typical flow: 1) share traffic profile and prompt set, 2) we spin a small dedicated pool or hosted variant for benchmarks, 3) run synthetic load for latency/cost and share results, 4) adjust model/quantization profile. timeline 1-2 weeks for initial bench.
05:38 Priya: that timeline works. cost sensitivity: our product team cares about cost per 1k tokens. do you provide tooling to tune quantization and batching?
05:45 Liam: Redwood Optimize will analyze workloads and recommend batching strategies, KV cache settings, and quantization profiles; we can project unit costs. We'll include an early optimization pass in the PoC.
05:56 Jenna: any gotchas when using proxy/gateway? e.g., double TLS, client certs, connection resets?
06:01 Tom: (interject) also, do you prefer long-lived connections or short-lived? our gateway currently tears down requests under 60s.
06:06 Rosa: streaming prefers long-lived connections (SSE or HTTP/2). If gateway tears down or has a proxy timeout, we recommend configuring it to allow longer durations for streaming. For non-streaming you can use request/response patterns. We also support chunked responses to mitigate proxy timeouts.
06:21 Liam: note on headers: pass x-client-id and x-request-id to keep correlation intact. We'll forward x-trace-id for internal tracing.
06:28 Priya: ok. final clarifying question: for LlamaIndex long-term indexing, is context window preserved across reruns? basically session affinity and kv cache behavior?
06:36 Liam: our runtime has KV cache management; session affinity is configurable. for Private/Dedicated you can pin cache sizes and TTLs. For Hosted we provide automatic prefix caching and you can set cache hints via metadata.
06:47 Sara: wrapping up - action items we'll follow up on are pricing/sizing, langchain examples, and your sample traffic. we'll set a PoC kickoff next week. anything else?
06:54 Jenna: please include security pack, SOC2, and KMS integration details. also a simple demo of the LangChain connector would help the team.
07:02 Sara: got it - i'll send pricing and security docs. liam will send code samples. thanks everyone. we'll schedule the PoC invite after we get the traffic profile.

End of transcript.
